name: 3attar
note: Gate 1 (Geography): 3attar is an Egyptian foodtech startup headquartered in Cairo/Maadi that raised its seed round in Egypt, not a Saudi-HQ'd entity. This is exactly the ICP's documented Egyptian-marketplace-mistagged-Saudi pattern; the Saudi delivery footprint does not establish in-country HQ.

name: 72Hair (sold via Beauty Steps Trading Co.)
note: 72hairsa.com redirects to beautysteps.sa, operated by Saudi-HQ'd Beauty Steps Trading Co., a live multi-brand dermocosmetics store with a real cart and large catalog. Beauty/cosmetics is approved; geography, channel, and scale hold.

name: A Market ماركت
note: Riyadh-HQ'd grocery e-commerce in the Al Othaim Markets lineage with live SAR checkout across a broad grocery catalog, loyalty program, and app. High-frequency approved category, clear in-country HQ.

name: aani-dani
note: Approved confectionery/F&B (chocolate/cake), stated Riyadh HQ, founded 1998, no red flags. Live site returned 503 to automated fetch (bot-block, not dead, confirmed by the identical 503 on a known-live chain), so per the ICP blocked-is-not-fail rule it passes; SKU-level scale was not independently re-verifiable this pass due to search-budget exhaustion.

name: abar
note: Bottled-water delivery app explicitly named as a confirmed Gate 5b app-download-rescue case in the locked ICP alongside Rasseed and ToYou, so the app path is pre-authorized regardless of the reason's hedge on an exact download figure.

name: Abdul Latif Jameel Electronics
note: Live Saudi electronics/appliances store with a working cart, SAR pricing, Saudi CR (4030031963) and VAT numbers, and showrooms in 5 cities. Evaluating the electronics-retail subsidiary on its own domain is correct under Gate 6 despite the automotive parent.

name: Abdullah Al-Othaim Markets
note: Major Tadawul-listed Saudi grocery/hypermarket chain headquartered in Riyadh. Approved high-frequency category with clear in-country HQ; a well-known real operator.

name: Abdullah Ali Al Amer & Brothers Trading Co
note: Live grocery-supermarket e-commerce on a dedicated shop subdomain, backed by ERP and a mobile app, HQ Al-Hofuf, Saudi Arabia. Approved category and confirmed transactional channel.

name: abdulsamadalqurashi
note: Root domain soft-404s but the live sa. subdomain is a large functioning Saudi oud/perfume store, re-gated per protocol. Famous Jeddah perfume house; perfume is an approved consumable, repeat-purchase category.

name: Abo Moati l ابو معطي
note: Independent check confirms a live consumer store at abomoati.com.sa (stationery, school supplies, toys, gifts) plus Nomu/Tadawul listing since 2017 and Riyadh HQ. The original reason's unconfirmed digital channel is now resolved as live; a wholesale arm exists but the consumer retail identity dominates.

name: actan
note: Riyadh-HQ'd women's fashion retailer with 26 KSA stores, 380k+ customers, and a live online store spanning dresses, jalabiyas, and matching sets. Broad seasonal assortment, so it passes Gate 3 rather than being narrow occasion-wear.

name: Adam Medical Company
note: Saudi online pharmacy with a large live catalog, real cart, and SAR pricing. Pharmacy retail is the explicit approved exception within health retail.

name: Ahmed Abdulwahed Company
note: Independent check resolves the distributor label: this is a genuine 54-showroom Saudi consumer-electronics retail chain (Jeddah HQ, founded 1960) with a tracked B2C e-commerce store and app, sales almost entirely in Saudi Arabia. Approved category, real channel, real scale.

name: ak
note: M.A. Al Abdul Karim & Co., a major Riyadh-HQ'd integrated fashion retailer (~$208M revenue, 1,010 staff, franchise brands Terranova/Calliope/RINA/Balabala) operating ak.com.sa as an online shopping platform. Approved category, substantial scale; the leftover-template artifact does not undercut a confirmed large retailer.

name: AL Asasyah Electronics Co Ltd
note: Corporate site leads to a live transactional storefront at al-asasyahonline.com with roughly 25 appliance/electronics subcategories, working cart, checkout, account, and wishlist. Broad multi-category retailer comfortably above the SKU floor.

name: Al Barakat Group Co Ltd.
note: Single-vertical eye/hearing-care retail group (not a mixed conglomerate); Barakat Optical is a live luxury eyewear store with 65+ showrooms and 80+ brands. Opticians are an explicitly approved category.

name: AL HAZMI STORES
note: Gate 4 (Digital channel): I loaded matajeralhazmi.sa and confirmed it is a corporate/store-locator site with About/Gallery/Careers and a sign-in but no products, prices, cart, or checkout, which refutes the substantiality basis for the prior Yes. A real Jizan grocery chain, but no live transactional store and no qualifying consumer app could be confirmed either way.

name: Al Majed for Oud الماجد للعود
note: Gate 6 (Duplicate-consolidation): this is the same company as entry #19 Al Majed Oud (almajed4oud.com), founded 1956 in Riyadh. It carries no domain of its own and must consolidate into that single account rather than stand as a separate Yes row.

name: Al Majed Oud.co
note: Al Majed for Oud, a Riyadh-HQ'd Saudi joint-stock oud/perfume retailer (est. 1956, Tadawul-listed, ~1,000 products, ~300 outlets) with a live regional online store. Approved consumable category; this is the surviving account of the #18/#19 duplicate pair.

name: Al Mujtama Pharmacy
note: Tadawul-listed Saudi multi-branch pharmacy chain running a Vue SPA storefront with SAMA-regulated Moyasar checkout and real product/cart code plus hundreds of branch references. Pharmacy is an explicitly approved recurring-purchase category.

name: Al Othaim Life
note: Major Saudi fashion group (Al Othaim), 27 brands across 370+ stores with omnichannel e-commerce on multiple online platforms. Independent check confirms the operation is fully launched, so the 'Unveiling Soon' page the original curl hit was a single sub-page, not the whole company; qualifies as a consolidated fashion-retail parent.

name: Al Wafa Hypermarket KSA
note: Multi-city Saudi hypermarket (Jeddah, Riyadh, Makkah, Dammam, Madina and more) with a live online platform, loyalty app, and broad grocery/general-merchandise range. The prior keyword-only reason holds up on independent check; approved high-frequency category.

name: al-araba
note: Gate 2 (Category): al-araba.com is AL ARABA Group, a Saudi vehicle-customizing and armoring business (maker of the 'Al Araba 1' car) with blog content on custom car interiors and luxury cars. Automotive is hard-excluded; the keyword-only cart/checkout pass was a false positive from a car-customization site.

name: AL-ASFOUR FURNITURE Co. Ltd.
note: Gate 2 (Category): Al Asfour is a furniture manufacturer producing/reconditioning ~1,000 units/day and supplying Aramco, SABIC Housing, and KAUST Housing via an institutional project-furnishing model. Manufacturing plus B2B project supply is hard-excluded even with a consumer showroom/installment arm.

name: Al-Dawaa Medical Services Co.
note: Saudi Arabia's largest pharmacy chain (500+ branches) with a live consumer store and iOS/Android apps. The given domain is the corporate/IR site for the same legal entity; the storefront runs at the sibling domain. Pharmacy approved.

name: Al-Maha Optical المها للبصريات
note: Independent check found the operator's site almahaopt.com.sa for a 115-store Riyadh-HQ'd optician chain (est. 1998, 160+ brands, 5,000+ SKUs of glasses/sunglasses/contact lenses). Opticians are approved and scale is clearly met; the site returned 503 to automated fetch (bot-block, not dead), but the business is strongly corroborated, so per the ICP blocked-is-not-fail rule the channel gate passes.

name: alabbasi
note: Saudi luxury fabric/textile retailer for garment-making, a vertical Gate 3 explicitly approves as high-frequency consumer retail; live store with a free-shipping threshold on a .sa domain. No B2B or manufacturing red flag in the consumer-facing operation.

name: alajlan
note: Gates 4 and 6: I loaded alajlan.com and it is the corporate portal of a diversified holding company (fashion plus real estate and contracting, hospitality, and corporate B2B) with no cart or checkout of its own, only links to brand social pages. It fails Gate 4 as a holding page with no own storefront and Gate 6 as a mixed conglomerate; the individual retail brands would each need a separate row.

name: alamal advanced medical
note: Distinct retail pharmacy chain (Al-Amal Pharmacies) with a live Shop Online app, Tabby BNPL and Google sign-in, and branches across 5 southwestern Saudi cities, separate from the parent's dental/medical clinics. Pharmacy retail is approved.

name: alamoudi
note: Saudi (Jizan) home-appliances/consumer-electronics retail chain since 1986 with an extensive live catalog, cart/account/wishlist infrastructure, and physical branches. Approved category, geography confirmed, scale above the SKU floor.

name: Alaryaf Sweets |  الارياف للحلويات
note: Gate 5 (Scale): the primary website is parked/dead and the branded ordering app's installs could not be confirmed at 50k+, the same dead-site-plus-sub-50k-app pattern the ICP ruled OUT for Al Sadhan. It is a real 45-year Qassim bakery/sweets chain but also runs 100+ B2B agents/distributors, so scale via a live digital channel is unconfirmable either way.

name: ALASEEL
note: Riyadh-HQ'd Arabic-apparel retailer (est. 1987) with stores in 9+ Saudi cities, a live store at alaseel.com.sa, and Amazon.sa/Noon presence across thobes, underwear, pajamas, and robes. Vertical integration does not disqualify a genuine multi-line apparel retailer, and thobes are daily-wear rather than narrow low-repeat.
